sentences.text: Rajesh Kumar vs . The Land Acquisition Officer, on 10 January,

2025 
Author: Sandeep Sharma
Bench: Sandeep Sharma
Rajesh Kumar Vs. The Land Acquisition Officer, Nhai and Others Cwp No.839 of 2025 10.01.2025
Present: Mr. Suneet Goel, Senior Advocate, with Mr. Vivek Negi and Mr. Purander Sharma,
Advocates, for the petitioner.

Mr. Rajan Kahol, Mr. Vishal Panwar and Mr. B.C. Verma, Additional Advocates General, with Mr.
Ravi Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General, for respondent No.1/State.
Cwp No.839 of 2025 Notice.
Mr. Rajan Kahol, learned Additional Advocate General, appears and waives service of notice on behalf of respondent No.1/State.

He prays for and is granted six weeks'
time to file reply.
Separate notices to respondents No.2 to 15 be issued, on taking steps within one week, returnable within six weeks.

Precisely, the grouse of the petitioner, as has been highlighted in the petition and further canvassed by Mr. Suneet Goel, learned Senior Counsel representing the applicant/petitioner is that since civil suit inter se petitioner and private-respondents No.2 to 15 for entitlement of compensation under National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, hereinafter, 'the Act'), was pending adjudication, there was no occasion, if any, for respondent No.1 to apply under Section 3H(4) of the Act to the learned Principal District Judge for apportionment, who despite having taken note of pendency of the civil suit inter se applicant/petitioner and private- respondents, proceeded to answer reference, thereby holding private-respondents entitled for entire amount of compensation.

Since it is apparent from the pleadings adduced on record that suit, on the issue of entitlement of compensation awarded under National Highways Act, is pending adjudication before the competent Court of law and such fact was brought to the notice of learned Reference Court in the proceedings initiated by respondent No.1 under Section 3H(4) of the Act, this Court deems it fit to order that till the next date of hearing, amount in terms of impugned award, shall not be disbursed, rather, same shall be kept in FDRs.
The application is disposed of with the direction to applicant/petitioner to file translated copies of documents in issue, within a period of four weeks.

January 10, 2025 (Sandeep Sharma),
